definitions.explanation: The part where string, rope, thread, or similar material has been tied together. Refers to the physical point of a knot.

examples.japanese: {結|むす}び{目|め}をしっかり{作|つく}った。
{結|むす}び{目|め}が{固|かた}くて{解|ほど}けない。
examples.english: The knot is too tight to untie.

examples.japanese: {靴紐|くつひも}の{結|むす}び{目|め}がほどけて、{何度|なんど}も{結|むす}び{直|なお}した。
examples.english: My shoelace knot kept coming undone, and I retied it many times.

notes:
USAGE:
A compound of {結|むす}ぶ (to tie) and {目|め} (point, spot). Refers specifically to the physical point where something is knotted. Used for ropes, strings, threads, shoelaces, and similar materials.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {結|むす}び{目|め}を{作|つく}る (to make a knot)
- {結|むす}び{目|め}を{解|ほど}く (to untie a knot)
- {結|むす}び{目|め}が{緩|ゆる}い (the knot is loose)
- {結|むす}び{目|め}が{固|かた}い (the knot is tight)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {結|むす}ぶ: to tie — the verb form, describes the action rather than the result
